title: AIDA implementation fix record
description: What `fix-record` verified for one fix round on one order, at <task folder>/implementation/fix-<unit_id>-<round>.json (ideal/implementation.md, 'The fix rounds re-run the first two checks'). One file per round, so a second round never overwrites the first and a person reading a stopped order can see both. The same shape as the build record with `round` in place of `attempt`, because the two steps verify the same code the same way and a reader who knows one must not have to learn another. Plain JSON, no fences, no markdown. A field present in a real record but absent from this schema's `properties` is a defect in the schema, not a value to silently accept, which is why `additionalProperties` is false.

schemaVersion.description: The shape this file was written in, the same field every other AIDA record carries.

takenAt.description: The UTC date this round was recorded, YYYY-MM-DD. Set by the script at the moment of writing, never typed by hand.

unit.description: The work order id this record belongs to, the same id `fix-brief` was given and the file's own basename encodes. Joined on, never re-minted.

startedAt.description: The commit this round began from, the full form of the `--started-at` value `fix-record` was given, resolved and confirmed to name a real commit in the code repository (exit 43 otherwise). The list in `commits` is read from here to `commit`.

commit.description: The code repository's HEAD at the moment `fix-record` ran, read fresh with `git rev-parse HEAD`, never assumed. A call on a round already recorded at this commit reports that record and records nothing twice.

commits.description: The commits the fixer made this round, full form, oldest first. `fix-record` derives it as `build-record` does: every commit from `startedAt` to `commit`, less each commit another order's records name. The owned-files check reads the files these commits change, and the round's diff holds these commits alone. `review-brief` reads it beside the build record's list.

round.description: Which fix round this is, one more than the ledger's own roundsUsed before this call. `fix-record` increments roundsUsed after writing this record, whether the checks below were met or not: a round is a fixer that ended, not a fixer that succeeded. The cap is FIX_ROUNDS_ALLOWED, two, and at the cap a round that did not pass stops the order.

reportPath.description: Where the fixer's own report lives, copied from `--report` as given. Only the path is kept here, never the report's content, for the same reason the build record keeps only a path: a fixer's account of what it did is never read as authority. A fixer reporting that its scope was too small is read by whichever mode is running, and that is the skill's conversation, not this file's.

diffPath.description: Where this round's own diff was written: the diff of the commits in `commits`. The verification reads its verdicts against this diff only, which is what keeps one round from growing into the next.

checks.description: The three deciding checks this step re-runs, the same checks in the same fixed order the build record holds them: the order's own proof, owned-files, frozen-tests.

executed.description: How many of the checks in `checks` actually executed: they ran a command, which is every check carrying an exitCode, or they computed a diff or a hash, which is owned-files and frozen-tests.

decidingChecks.description: States plainly which of the deciding checks ideal/implementation.md names this step ran. All three, and the field exists so a reader never has to count `checks` to learn what a pass here covered.

total.description: The number of deciding checks in total. Always 3, the same constant the build record carries.

ranHere.description: The `id` of each check in `checks`, in the same order, copied rather than re-derived.

recheckedAt.description: Present only after `go-on --continue check` ran this round's checks again over its own range, with no fixer dispatched and no round spent (gap row 310): the UTC date of that run, YYYY-MM-DD. `checks`, `executed` and `decidingChecks` then hold that run's answers; `round`, `startedAt`, `commit` and `takenAt` stay the round's own.

checksBefore.description: Present with `recheckedAt`: the checks the second run replaced, id and verdict only, as build-record-schema.json keeps them.

check.description: The same check object build-record writes. One definition, in build-record-schema.json, because both steps run the same checks through the same function.
